extracted.intended_audience: reviewers for CVPR 2025 (paper reviewers, program committee members)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for reviewing CVPR 2025 submissions: what reviewers should check, ethical/procedural rules, how to write helpful reviews, and how to treat policy/technical edge cases (datasets, supplementary material, arXiv, LLM use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance: technical soundness and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper that is accepted should be technically sound and make a contribution to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for what is good or stimulating in the paper, and what knowledge advance it has made. Weigh novelty and potential impact alongside reported performance. The fact that a proposed method does not exceed state-of-the-art accuracy on an existing benchmark dataset is not grounds for rejection by itself. Embrace novel, brave concepts even if not tested on many datasets. Minor flaws that can be easily corrected should not be a reason to reject a paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific and detailed in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Your discussion, more than your score, will help authors, fellow reviewers, and Area Chairs understand the basis for your recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take time to write thoughtful, detailed reviews; short reviews are unhelpful. Bullet lists with one short sentence per bullet are NOT a detailed review. Include specific feedback on ways the authors can improve their papers and point to particular sections that are unclear with suggestions for clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect anonymity in the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not take active steps to discover the identity of the authors, and make all efforts to keep their own identity invisible to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may post preprints on arXiv; that does not automatically disqualify reviewing. If you happen to know or suspect the authors' identities, still attempt to be impartial. If you do not know identities at the start, DO NOT attempt to find them by searching the web for preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect ideas / confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect the confidentiality of ideas represented in submitted papers; CVPR submissions are not published documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not show the paper, results, videos/images, code or supplementary material to anyone else unless they are asked to help write a review. Do not use ideas/code from papers you review to develop your own ideas/code. After the review process, destroy all copies of papers and supplementary material and erase any code and implementations or results you created to evaluate the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest (COI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid any conflict of interest; there should be no question about the impartiality of a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviewing would create a possible conflict, return the paper and do not submit a review. Conflicts include (but are not limited to): working at the same institution as an author; being directly involved in the work or receiving credit; membership of an author's thesis committee on related thesis work; collaboration in the past three years (e.g., co-authored papers/grants); being an advisor or advisee (treat advisees as possible lifetime conflicts—CVPR historically more flexible but exercise caution); situations others might perceive as a conflict. If in doubt, contact the Area Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be professional and constructive in tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a courteous, informative, incisive, and helpful review; avoid belittling or sarcastic comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrase criticisms constructively while being honest. Avoid referring to authors in the second person ('you'). It is best to avoid the term 'the authors' as well; instead use the third person ('the paper'). Be generous with suggestions for improvement: new technical tools, datasets, application areas, or ways to generalize the idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check your assignment for conflicts and competence
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as you get your reviewing assignment, ensure you have no obvious conflict of interest and that you feel comfortable reviewing the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If issues arise (conflict or discomfort with topic/expertise), contact the Area Chair right away as instructed in assignment emails so they can reassign the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know and follow author and conference policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should read the Author Guidelines carefully to familiarize themselves with official policies authors are expected to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you suspect a policy violation, contact the Chairs. In the meantime, proceed with your review assuming no violation has taken place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims of prior work / novelty must be supported
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in a review that the submitted work 'has been done before' MUST be backed up with specific references and an explanation of how closely they are related.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For positive reviews, explicitly summarize what novel aspects are most interesting in the Strengths section. Unsupported, vague claims about prior work are unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of arXiv prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are not required to discuss and compare their work with recent arXiv reports, and failing to cite or beat an arXiv paper should not by itself be grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should use judgment: authors should properly acknowledge sources that directly and obviously inspired them. Reviewers may suggest authors acknowledge or be aware of relevant arXiv work. If plagiarism or academic dishonesty is suspected, bring concerns to the Program Chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary material is intended to provide derivation details and results that do not fit within the paper's space limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult supplementary only if it helps to understand the paper and its contribution. Supplementary MAY NOT include results obtained with an improved version of the method (e.g., following additional parameter tuning or training), or an updated/corrected submission PDF. If the supplementary violates guidelines, contact the Area Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal-phase requests and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may request clarifications, additional illustrations, or small experiments reasonably run within the rebuttal period, but should not request substantial additional experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per PAMI-TC motion, do not request substantial additional experiments in rebuttal or penalize lack of them. 'Substantial' refers to what would be needed in a major revision. The rebuttal may include figures or comparison tables of results reported in the submission/supplemental material or other papers. Papers should not be penalized for supplying extra results in rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling withdrawn datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a withdrawn dataset (e.g., DukeMTMC-ReID, MS-Celeb-1M) is not in itself grounds for rejection but should invite close scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag such cases in the review form for AC/PC consideration. Consider: Do the authors explain why they used it? Is the explanation compelling? Is there a reasonable alternative dataset? Authors may be unaware the dataset was withdrawn. If the paper could be accepted without experiments on the withdrawn dataset, advise authors to remove those experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers must not require comparison to withdrawn datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a violation of policy for a reviewer or Area Chair to require comparison on a dataset that has been withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not request such comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating dataset claims as contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission claims a dataset as one of its contributions, there should be a reasonable expectation that the dataset will be made publicly available upon publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private or restricted datasets are not grounds for rejection, but they cannot be claimed as contributions in their own right. Evaluate such papers on their other technical merits and use judgment about the dataset claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting comparisons to closed-source / non-public work
rubrics_metrics.description: When a requested comparison requires re-implementation because code/data/pretrained models are not publicly available, such a request should be appropriately justified if used as a basis for a paper decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: minor changes to an already implemented method with available code, or where re-implementation is common practice in the sub-field. Comparisons should only be requested if the publication/code has been available sufficiently ahead of the submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: No minimum acceptance quota
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no minimum number of papers a reviewer should accept or reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate each paper on its own merits. If most papers assigned to you seem acceptable, accept them; if you believe most are poor, provide clear and very specific comments in each review. Do NOT assume your assigned stack should match the overall conference acceptance rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not ask authors to cite your papers to reveal identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not give away your identity by asking the authors to cite several of your own papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid self-serving citation requests; they risk revealing reviewer identity and are inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/out-of-scope handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If you think the paper is out of scope for CVPR's subject areas, clearly explain why in the review and suggest other publication venues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the mismatch is extreme, keep an open mind because the conference aims for a diverse set of good papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be generous with improvement suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide authors with new ideas for how they can improve their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest technical tools, datasets to try, application areas, or ways to generalize ideas to increase impact. Constructive suggestions are highly valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM (large language model) policy for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Large language models (LLMs) are NOT allowed to be used for writing the reviews nor the meta-reviews at any step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot use an LLM to write content for your review or meta-review, nor share substantial content from the paper or your review with an LLM (e.g., for translation). You may use LLMs for background research or to check short phrases for clarity. Grammar-checker software that may have used LLMs is allowed. Enforcement: (Senior) ACs will check (meta-)reviews for LLM policy violations; flagged reviews enter an oversight process; if found highly irresponsible, papers submitted by the reviewer may be desk rejected at PCs' discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling social-media disclosures about submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: A social-media post sharing information on a CVPR submission without authors being involved does not by itself signal a policy violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A violation occurs only when authors are proactively sharing the submission publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review impact on reviewer reputation / incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Thoughtful, helpful reviews benefit authors and reviewers; Area Chairs know reviewer identities and your identity will be visible to other reviewers after decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being a helpful reviewer generates goodwill and may help you be recognized (e.g., Outstanding Reviewer). This is an encouragement to be constructive, but not a rule for evaluation.
